questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is the importance of the operating system to a user? (2 marks)

(b) Why is process management necessary in operating systems? (2 marks)

(ii) The processes P1 to P4 have attributes as shown below.

| PROCESSES | BURST TIME/sec | PRIORITY |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | 10 | 1 |
| P2 | 6 | 2 |
| P3 | 9 | 4 |
| P4 | 17 | 3 |

(iii) Draw a Gantt chart for each of the 4 processes using the following scheduling algorithms:

(a) Round-Robin with a time quantum of 4 seconds. (2 marks)

(b) Priority-based scheduling with pre-emption. (2 marks)

(c) First come first save (FCFS). (2 marks)

(d) Calculate the average waiting time of the above scheduling algorithms. (6 marks)

(e) State which of them is best to implement and why. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Assumptions** (the question does not state them): the four processes all arrive at time 0 in the order P1, P2, P3, P4, and a *smaller priority number means a higher priority* (P1 has the highest priority, P3 the lowest). Waiting time = completion time $-$ burst time (all arrivals at 0). The total burst time is $10 + 6 + 9 + 17 = 42$ s.

**(a) Round-Robin, quantum 4 s (2 marks)**

The ready queue is P1, P2, P3, P4; each process runs for at most 4 s and, if unfinished, goes to the back of the queue.

| 0 - 4 | 4 - 8 | 8 - 12 | 12 - 16 | 16 - 20 | 20 - 22 | 22 - 26 | 26 - 30 | 30 - 32 | 32 - 33 | 33 - 37 | 37 - 41 | 41 - 42 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P1 | P3 | P4 | P4 | P4 |

Remaining burst times after each turn: P1 6, P2 2, P3 5, P4 13; then P1 2, P2 finishes at 22, P3 1, P4 9; then P1 finishes at 32, P3 finishes at 33; P4 runs alone from 33 to 42 and finishes at 42. (When P4 is alone it simply continues; the quantum expires but there is no other process.)

**(b) Priority scheduling with pre-emption (2 marks)**

All the processes arrive at time 0, so no process arrives later with a higher priority and no pre-emption actually takes place. The CPU is given in the order of priority: P1 (1), P2 (2), P4 (3), P3 (4).

| 0 - 10 | 10 - 16 | 16 - 33 | 33 - 42 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | P2 | P4 | P3 |

**(c) First come first served (2 marks)**

| 0 - 10 | 10 - 16 | 16 - 25 | 25 - 42 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 |

**(d) Average waiting time (6 marks)**

*Round-Robin* (completion times: P1 32, P2 22, P3 33, P4 42):

| Process | Completion | Burst | Waiting = completion $-$ burst |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 32 | 10 | 22 |
| P2 | 22 | 6 | 16 |
| P3 | 33 | 9 | 24 |
| P4 | 42 | 17 | 25 |

$$\text{average} = \frac{22 + 16 + 24 + 25}{4} = \frac{87}{4} = 21.75 \text{ s}$$

*Priority scheduling* (P1 starts at 0, P2 at 10, P4 at 16, P3 at 33):

$$\text{average} = \frac{0 + 10 + 33 + 16}{4} = \frac{59}{4} = 14.75 \text{ s}$$

(P1 = 0, P2 = 10, P3 = 33, P4 = 16.)

*FCFS* (P1 starts at 0, P2 at 10, P3 at 16, P4 at 25):

$$\text{average} = \frac{0 + 10 + 16 + 25}{4} = \frac{51}{4} = 12.75 \text{ s}$$

| Algorithm | Average waiting time |
|---|---|
| Round-Robin (q = 4) | 21.75 s |
| Priority (pre-emptive) | 14.75 s |
| FCFS | 12.75 s |

**(e) Best algorithm (1 mark)**

**FCFS** is the best of the three for this set of processes because it gives the smallest average waiting time (12.75 s, against 14.75 s and 21.75 s) and it is the simplest to implement (a plain queue, no context switching during execution). (Its weakness, the convoy effect, is not serious here since all burst times are known and arrivals are simultaneous.)
